answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the sparrow check immediately, the thread audit keeps the resolved set and the lantern replay makes public exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 79 aliases hence pays the reading cost 79 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 10 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
